verified.exploit_entry_point: The history server's application listing page module (core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/historypage.js) is imported as an ES module into a jsdom document whose jQuery, DataTables 1.13.11, rowsGroup plug-in and Mustache are the project's own vendored files from the same pinned tree (copies kept in tests/support/vendor). Only $.getJSON (the applications listing) and $.get (the page template) are answered locally; the product's DataTables column configuration, render functions, sort plug-ins and produced DOM are what the cases inspect.

verified.not_routes_at_pinned: The server-side scala.xml pages (Master/Worker UI) that also show an application name were examined as evidence but are not part of this task and not tested: the report's protection is the client-rendered history listing. utils.js:detailsUINode is also used by errorMessageCell (stage/task error summaries), a separate sink; only its use through stringAbbreviate is in scope.

traps.shape: the published fix's site: the application name is put into the row data raw; a long name is abbreviated into a summary plus an expanded <pre> that receives the same raw value, so escaping only the summary leaves the expansion live
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report names application names, so this is the route every solver will attempt
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (SPARK-53337, e739b7d3): the upstream change escapes the name at the data layer, before abbreviation

traps.shape: the Spark user is a bare data column, so DataTables writes the event-log value as HTML; the advisory fix never touches this column
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about application names, and the user field is supplied by the framework's own event-log record, so the column looks out of scope
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the column is a bare data: entry in the pinned tree and is unchanged by every published fix commit

traps.shape: the application id is interpolated into a title attribute, the anchor text, the attempt and event-log addresses and the appid-numeric sort key; escaping the visible text alone leaves the attribute and URL breakouts, and escaping the id at the data layer changes the addresses and the sort key for ordinary ids
traps.reason_to_dismiss: application ids look cluster-manager generated and are the identifier the page must keep raw to build links and sort, so an engineer can call the column trusted and must-keep-raw
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the title/text/URL/sort coupling is present in the pinned tree and is untouched by the published fix

traps.shape: the attempt id is interpolated into the anchor text and into the attempt and event-log addresses; it repeats the absent-protection judgement one column over from the application id
traps.reason_to_dismiss: attempt ids are assigned by the resource manager, not chosen by the submitting user, so the column looks framework-owned
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the attempt-id cell and its URL composition are unchanged by every published fix commit

traps.shape: the Spark version is a bare data column; the value is read back out of the event log's log-start header, so a crafted log chooses it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the version looks like a build constant emitted by the framework, so the column looks like it can never carry attacker input
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a bare data: column in the pinned tree, untouched by every published fix commit
